messages:
Sasha M: Heads up — TuneBox (customer) opened a high-sev ticket: widespread 504s from hosted API since 03:07 UTC. They report p95 request latency jumping from ~300ms to 4-6s then 504. Ticket attached: https://support.example/t/4532. Request IDs: r-9a3f, r-9a40, r-9a42.

Tom B: saw same in metrics — request_queue_depth for the cluster spiked to 18k, continuous-batcher backlog grew, dequeue rate dropped. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/boards/queue?from=03:00&to=03:20

Mei L: logs show a lot of requests stuck in batching waiting state, kv-cache cold misses increased. Many requests had long scheduling wait times before being batched. Paste of sample traces: 
```
batcher: enqueue wait=4200ms, batch_size=1, tenant=tunebox
runtime: kv_warm=false, kernel_sel=fp16, exec_ms=120
gateway: resp_status=504, reason=queue_timeout
```

Devon R: Looks like the continuous batching loop couldn't keep up with a sudden burst of small requests, queue depth cap kicked in and we started dropping at router. Can anyone confirm router logs for early_rejects?

ops-bot: alert(ingress-high-queue): cluster=eu-west-1, peak_queue=18123, early_rejects=327, p95_latency=6000ms.

AJ K: Repro steps I ran locally against a small canary: send 2k concurrent tiny prompts (len<=16) to hosted endpoint -> queue depth climbs, batcher keeps forming tiny batches and CPU on batcher nodes pegged. I could reproduce 504s when queue_depth > 8k and dequeue latency > 2s.

Sasha M: Customer says the errors started after a sudden campaign spike (they sent 50k inference calls in 10 minutes). They are asking for mitigation and ETA.

Tom B: Short-term mitigation: increase per-cluster max_queue_depth and throttle that tenant via rate-limiter. I can push a temporary tenant-rate cap to 200 qps for TuneBox — reduces load and gives time to drain. Anyone object?

Mei L: +1 for tenant throttle. Also recommend applying batching size floor (min_batch_size=8) for this model so small requests get coalesced rather than forming single-item batches. That reduces kernel overhead.

Devon R: Two operational actions: 1) throttle tenant (Tom) 2) switch the tenant to model-variant small-quant (fallback) to lower per-token run time while we drain. I can create a routing override for the tenant.

AJ K: Note: fallback to smaller model reduces quality but will cut exec_ms ~40% in our perf sims. Need customer consent. I can prepare an opt-in text for support.

Rachel C: I'll coordinate with TuneBox PM/legal for consent. Meanwhile I'm adding a Priority:High comment to the ticket and telling them we're throttling to reduce errors.

Tom B: I've applied tenant throttle -> tunebox.rate_limit=200 qps at 03:12:45 UTC. Early rejects dropped 70% within 60s, queue started draining.

Mei L: I pushed batching policy override for model=redwood-serve/v1: set min_batch_bytes=1024 and min_batch_items=6 for tenant. That should force coalescing.

Devon R: Routing override in place to fallback->redwood-serve/v1-small-quant for tenant at 03:14:10 UTC. Monitoring impact.

AJ K: After changes, p95 dropped to ~450ms, error rate to ~0.8% (was 12%). Will watch for KV cache warm-up for the next 15 min.

Sasha M: Customer updated: saw immediate improvement, thanks. They want postmortem and permanent fixes.

Mei L: Action items for postmortem: 1) improve continuous-batcher admission control to prefer coalescing small requests 2) auto-trigger tenant throttles on observed queue growth > 5k 3) evaluate per-tenant warmup (prefetch KV) for sudden spikes 4) revisit default max_queue_depth per cluster.

Devon R: I'll open an infra ticket to add an automated mitigation runbook (throttle+fallback+batching-policy) and a toggle in Console for on-call to apply quickly.

Tom B: Marking incident resolved for now — moving to follow-up RFC. Closing slack thread after we confirm postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
